questions.stem: A probe moves at 0.327c relative to a station, and a particle is fired forward at 0.851c relative to the probe. What is the particle's speed relative to the station, in units of c?

options.misconception: Adds speeds with Galilean arithmetic, ignoring the c^2 denominator
Uses a minus sign in the velocity-addition denominator
Reports the product of the speeds instead of their combination

questions.hint: Use u = (u' + v)/(1 + u'v/c^2), and keep the plus sign in the denominator.

questions.stem: Two beams approach each other, each moving at 0.203c and 0.731c relative to the lab in opposite directions. What is the speed of one beam as seen from the other, in units of c?

options.misconception: Adds speeds with Galilean arithmetic, ignoring the c^2 denominator
Reports the product of the two speeds instead of their combination
Uses a minus sign in the velocity-addition denominator

questions.explanation: In the rest frame of one beam the other approaches at (a + b)/(1 + ab) = (0.203 + 0.731)/(1 + 0.1484) = 0.813c. Adding naively can exceed c, subtracting gives their lab-frame separation rate, and the wrong-sign denominator also breaks the light-speed limit.
questions.hint: Use the relativistic relative-speed formula with both speeds positive.
